Connor —

Thanks for the recap and for jumping on this. Couple of notes from our side that might help with repro: we are using the Redwood JS SDK 1.3.2 with a short-lived JWT rotated every 5 minutes via our auth service. We put an NGINX reverse proxy in front of the service (basic proxy, no buffering). Failures are most common when the request payload exceeds ~120KB.

Repro info attached: acme_sdk_error_log.txt contains a 502 response with the following snippet (extracted):
- status: 502
- path: /v1/structured_call
- message: upstream prematurely closed connection
- client-ip: 198.51.100.42

Curl we used to reproduce:
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/structured_call -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @postcall_sample_payload.json

We attached postcall_sample_payload.json (a reduced version that still triggers the failure). Happy to pair; our devs are available tomorrow afternoon PST.

— Sam Torres
Lead Engineer, Integrations | Acme Retail

Thanks Sam — this is very helpful. I dug into the logs you sent. Initial observations and immediate tries you can run client-side to help isolate: 

1) Client timeout vs server processing: increase your client-side HTTP timeout to 90s to rule out proxy timeouts (NGINX default proxy_read_timeout is 60s in many configs).
2) Chunking/content-length: the SDK sends payloads as application/json with Content-Length; please try sending the same payload with curl using --header 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' to see if the proxy behaves differently.
3) SDK header: enable debug flag in the SDK and set x-rdwd-client-version header (we added extra logging server-side for >=1.4.0). If possible, test briefly with a patched SDK build I will provide.

I will open INF-2027 in our tracker and assign to SRE for a deeper look (link below). For immediate repro steps on our side I will:
- reproduce the exact payload in a sandbox with the same 1.3.2 runtime and NGINX in front,
- capture tcpdump between the proxy and Redwood to confirm whether upstream connection is closed by our runtime or the proxy.

Can you confirm:
- exact SDK snippet (npm package name and version string),
- whether you use connection pooling across requests or recreate the HTTP client per call,
- whether any middleware rewrites headers.

I will also prepare a short patch for the SDK that adds a diagnostic header and toggles our internal KV-cache behavior; if that reproduces we can roll a canary. ETA for initial repro + SRE triage: 24-48 hours.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
